fixes.explanation: Verse 30 puts it in order. As soon as Laban, Rebekah's brother, saw the ring and the bracelets on his sister's wrists, and heard her words, he went and found the man. I think a brother who spots jewelry on his sister's wrists is going to get moving. Ring first, then he goes to find the man.

Hold on, baker, this one is True. Verse 30 says that as soon as Laban, Rebekah's brother, saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister's wrists, and heard Rebekah's words, he went and found the man standing by the camels near the spring. Jewelry first, then the brother shows up. I think that's the fastest anyone has ever gone from 'nice bracelet' to 'who is this guy?'
Laban says, “Come, you who are blessed by the LORD…” (verse 31). That's how he greets a stranger standing out by a spring with his camels. Not a bad welcome for a man who just showed up.

Right, the opposite is true. Laban says, “Why are you standing out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.” (verse 31). The house is ready before the man says a word about why he came. Then the camels are unloaded, and straw and feed are brought to them (verse 32). I think Laban would pass any surprise-guest test.

Nice try, but no name gets asked here. In verse 47 the servant asks, “Whose daughter are you?” Rebekah answers, “The daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.” He wants to know her family, and only then do the ring and bracelets go on.

Verse 53 says he brought out jewels of silver and gold, and articles of clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and her mother. Rebekah's gifts get named first, though. That's a lot of unwrapping for one family.

Gifts for her father don't come up. Rebekah's brother and mother say, “Let the girl remain with us ten days or so. After that, she may go.” (verse 55). The gifts in this scene go to Rebekah, her brother and her mother (verse 53). What they ask for here is time.

Land and gold aren't in their words. Verse 60 says, “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your offspring possess the gates of their enemies.” The silver and gold came earlier, from the servant's gifts (verse 53). The blessing is about her children.

The jar belongs to the spring scene, where she carried it on her shoulder (verse 45). Here, verse 65 says, “So she took her veil and covered herself.” By now she has gotten down from her camel and asked who that man in the field is (verse 64). So no jar this time, just a veil.

No staff in this scene. After the servant says, “It is my master…” verse 65 says, “So she took her veil and covered herself.” She had gotten down from her camel and asked who the man in the field was (verse 64). The veil is the thing the text names.

Hold on, this one is True. Verse 61 says Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So she isn't heading out on her own. I think that's a nice way to start a long trip, with company.
